design_rationale:
WORKLOG — task 1 (window_contract_deposits_and_cancellations). Revision 9 (policy-task audit rounds 1–8 and render-source round 1 closed; see [Revisions]).

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 1: {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 6]}. Deposit balance (root, owner=user pay_deposit_balance_19bfa79b) 4 factors; door bundle discount credit (post_door_bundle_credit_ed16c33c) 6 factors. Task 0 holds the payoff, late charge, change-order fee and remeasure fee; scopes are disjoint and cover all six policies. One edge, value_input.

[Why it is a good test] Elena asks only to pay what is left of her window deposit by card. The number (1719.48) needs reading the deposit rule's prerequisite sentence, finding her paired door contract under the stage-by-stage pairing terms (her only door contract, measured, signed 41 days before the windows, not cancelled; discount program none), seeing that the window ledger lacks the window side's bundle credit while the door ledger already shows the door's own 214.00 credit (near-miss), figuring the credit through six factors (161.27), then the deposit on the measured value net of that credit with the upfront shares and the size step.

[Problem-tree card] root window_ext_deposit_balance -> window_ext_door_bundle_credit, value_input, gate measured_value, form state. Sentence (negated direction), identical to the edge's condition: "The deposit balance is not worked out until the ledger carries this contract's door bundle discount credit whenever a door contract of the household pairs with this contract under the window-side bundle pairing terms and this contract's discount program is none." The bundle-credit rule grants the window side's credit once per window contract, and for a household holding exactly one door contract that is not cancelled (this household) the policy pairs the window contract with that door when it was signed within the 60-day window and both discount programs are none, so the sentence asks for exactly one credit; only the bundle-credit policy books door bundle discount credits. False at frozen_time: no price credit on the window ledger. Step 8 books 161.27; measured value 15336.00 -> 15174.73; skipping it gives 1759.80. user_scenario never mentions a discount, credit or bundle; tools validate nothing.

[Base-invariant card] Step 8, subject window_price_credit: window_price_credits.bundle_vs_program (discount program none). Step 10, subject window_payment_received: window_agg_payment_application, window_booking_deposit, window_final_balance -> policy_scope. No time gate. Overwrites: price_credits 'A door_bundle_discount credit equals the series bundle percentage of the signed contract price' (rate x credit basis) and the grant clause 'it is granted on the window contract when the customer signs a Ridgeline door contract within the bundle window ... and neither contract is cancelled, and once per pair of contracts' (window side: once per window contract, paired with the door carrying the most recent door-side window bundle discount when that door is not cancelled, its program is none and it is in the window; other doors earn their discount on the door side only); grant timing and the program gate kept. booking_deposit cash and financed sentences (measured value; the financed replaced_by names its scope).

[Business-object card] Target RW-26-131058 (W1), the household's only window contract. Paired door RD-26-137715. Measured value = 11284.00 + oversize 192.00 + the one customer change order of 2026-09-15 (color 1652.00, grilles 416.00, triple pane 1792.00; within the 2200 free count of 1) - credit 161.27. Payments counted: the 3385.20 deposit.

[Factor card — bundle credit 161.27, all-baseline 451.36] bundle_credit_basis (method, cross door): door signed first -> window product only, 748.00 x 14 confirmed openings = 10472.00 vs signed price 11284.00 -> 173.77. door_project_step (cross door): 4280.00 -> +0.01 -> 131.95. window_project_step: 14 openings confirmed -> +0.005 -> 146.61. bundle_timing_share: 41 days -> 0.7 -> 230.38. promo_financing_share (multi-source window plan OR door plan, cross finance): door on Same-As-Cash 18 -> 0.5 -> 322.54. door_commitment_share (cross door): measured -> 0.8 -> 201.59.
[Factor card — deposit balance 1719.48, all-baseline 1167.22] deposit_method (method): cash with color and oversize lines -> 0.25 x value + upfront shares; standard -> 408.48. deposit_size_step: 15174.73 in [15000, 25000) -> 0.05 -> 2390.82. special_order_upfront_share: color -> 1.0 -> 480.48. oversize_upfront_share: 2 oversize -> 0.5 -> 1647.48. Near-miss: the credit leaves the value just above 15000; grilles and triple pane are not special-order lines.

[Seed card] Elena Dorsey (phone 5135550113, email elena.dorsey1@gmail.com, ZIP 45208, DOB 1971-09-30, profile opened 2026-07-21 with the door purchase). Door: Glide 840 at 4280.00, 15% financed deposit 642.00 on Tue 2026-07-21, measured 2026-08-04, Same-As-Cash 18 approved for 3638.00 (unfunded until completion), door-side window bundle credit 214.00 granted Mon 2026-08-31. Window W1: in-home Mon 2026-08-31, deposit 3385.20 (0.30 x 11284.00, this charter's rule at signing), measured 2026-09-11. Nothing else lit.

[Persona] Brisk hospital pharmacist; volunteers the goal and the salesperson's remark that the color upgrade needs more down; identity details only when asked; door contract number and its financing on request; passive agreement if told something must be put on the account first; pays exactly the quoted amount by debit card; ends.

[Standard solution] locate (0), verify (1); window contracts (2), window ledger (3), door contracts (4, pairing), door ledger (5), financing accounts (6); grant credit 161.27 (7-8); hand over; she pays 1719.48 by card (9-10).

[Verification runs] Gold replayed with the real tools; handling-time evaluation with check_compute's functions; a scan with rounding switched off finds no exact half cent in gold, factor-baseline or all-baseline figures (161.2688; 5104.6825). credit 161.27 (173.77/131.95/146.61/230.38/322.54/201.59; all 451.36); deposit 1719.48 (408.48/2390.82/480.48/1647.48; all 1167.22); skip credit -> 1759.80.

[Revisions] Round 1: timing share cross_difficulty null; financed overwrite quote fixed; record primitives in the deposit factors; a tautological condition removed. Round 2: bundle_rate_source (a rate choice) replaced by the bundle_credit_basis method; G2 sentence/condition carry the base grant conditions; ties removed (timing 0.7, measured door 0.8); G8 scoped replaced_by; the product basis reads the final measure's confirmed openings. Round 3: G9 wording. Round 4 (audit revision_3, G13/T1-3): the window side's credit is now once per window contract, paired with the household's door contract whose booking deposit was received most recently (an old out-of-window door can never be picked over a newer one; two in-window doors need only one window-side credit, so the credit tool's row id cannot collapse a second needed write); the compute reads that door everywhere (signing date, price, stage, financing), the deposit sentence and condition ask for exactly that one credit, and 'and once per pair of contracts' is declared as overwritten for the window side. Registration observation: the returning-owner step (which had to pick among several registrations) is replaced by window_project_step (openings confirmed at the final measure), so no registration is read; the 2018 window project (contract, ledger, order, job, registration) and its three reads are removed from the seed and gold as they no longer feed any decision, and the persona's 2018 mention is dropped. Scored values changed: credit 175.93 -> 161.27, deposit 1715.82 -> 1719.48; GT re-indexed (credit call step 11 -> 8, payment step 13 -> 10). Tool signatures unchanged.

[Closure] bundle credit -> post_door_bundle_credit_ed16c33c -> step 8 amount 161.27 -> door_bundle_discount credit row; deposit -> pay_deposit_balance_19bfa79b -> step 10 amount 1719.48 -> booking_deposit payment row. charter_scope = computations = required_documents.
[Draft recomputation from the visible context] From the deposit rule and its sentence, the bundle-credit rule and ladders and share-tool returns: paired door = RD-26-137715, window credit missing -> 161.27; deposit on 15174.73 -> 1719.48; no alternative reading found.
[Hard spots] taking the door ledger credit as the window credit; figuring the credit on the signed price although the door led; forgetting the deferred-interest promotion on the door plan; figuring the deposit before the credit (1759.80); counting grilles/triple pane as special-order lines.

[Revisions — round 5] (audit revision_4, G14/T1-4, G15, G17) Pairing by the latest booking deposit is withdrawn: it contradicted the kept base grant clause (financed doors with no deposit, a later out-of-window door, a cancelled latest door) and is not how a contractor pairs a bundle. The window-side grant clause is now declared as overwritten in full and replaced by a pairing among door contracts signed within the 60-day window of this contract, chosen stage by stage (signed, measured, ordered, installed, closed; at each stage the door contract entered first in the records, which is the earliest signed since contracts are entered at signing; cancelled doors never pair); the compute reads exactly that sequence (one first-entered door per stage, each tested against the window by DAYS) and figures nothing when none pairs. G15: the per-stage tie-break is stated (first entered). G17: the window-project step reads the completed final measure's confirmed openings (the largest count should more than one be recorded) instead of a sum. The deposit sentence and condition were rewritten to ask for this contract's credit whenever a door pairs under those terms (identical texts). Every scored value (161.27, 1719.48), every factor-baseline and all-baseline figure and the GT steps are unchanged on this world; tool signatures unchanged.

[Revisions — round 6] (audit revision_5, G18 and the class sweep) The pairing no longer depends on record order anywhere. For each stage a door contract can be at (signed, measured, ordered, installed, closed) the household's latest-signed door contract at that stage is taken (XLATEST over door contracts on signed_date with a status filter); those signed within the 60-day window of this contract are candidates; the latest-signed candidate pairs, ties going to the stage further along and then the highest contract price (XMAX); cancelled doors are never taken; no candidate -> no window-side credit. The window and door financing reads take the account in force (approved/active/delinquent/paid off). Probe table (scratch copies, decoy entered ahead of the real record): out-of-window measured door (2025-01-10) -> credit 161.27 (unchanged); earlier in-window measured door (2026-07-05) -> 161.27; later in-window cancelled door -> 161.27; same-day measured door at a lower price -> 161.27; a later in-window door at the signed stage (2026-08-10) -> 259.18 (it is the latest-signed candidate and pairs, by the rule); no door -> 0; cancelled zero-interest door account first -> 161.27; no door account -> 322.54. Stated limit of the compute language (no time window anchored on another record's date): a door contract signed more than 60 days after this contract, at the same stage as an in-window door, is the one taken at that stage, so the in-window door at that stage is not a candidate (probe: a measured door signed 2026-12-01 -> no credit); such a door can only exist when the credit is figured more than 60 days after this contract was signed, after the bundle window has closed, and the rule states this outcome exactly. Every scored value (161.27, 1719.48), every figure and the GT steps are unchanged; tool signatures unchanged.

[Revisions — round 7] (audit revision_6, G18; coordinator route-around) The window side no longer re-derives the bundle window over all door contracts. It pairs with the door contract carrying the household's most recent window bundle discount granted on the door side under the door terms (door_transactions, door_price_credit, credit_kind window_bundle_discount, selected by XLATEST on txn_date, ties on date by the highest amount via XMAX), so it pairs the door the door side itself granted. That door pairs only when it is not cancelled, its discount program is none and its signing date lies within 60 days of this contract's signing date (DAYS between the two specific dates); otherwise, or with no door-side credit, no window-side credit arises (rule states it). Seed realism: the door charter grants the door-side credit when the customer signs a window contract within the bundle window; RD-26-137715 was signed first (2026-07-21), so its credit arises at the window signing, 2026-08-31, for 0.05 x 4280.00 = 214.00 with discount program none; that row was already seeded at that date and amount. Nothing else reads it: only the pairing bindings read door_transactions; the factors read the paired door contract's fields and the deposit reads only the window ledger. Probe table (scratch copies, decoy rows entered first): gold -> credit 161.27, deposit 1719.48; old out-of-window door credit (2018 door, 2018 credit) -> 161.27; cancelled door with a later credit (2026-09-20) -> 0 (the most recent credit's door is cancelled, so by the rule no window-side credit; stated limit); second door credited the same day at a lower amount -> 161.27; second in-window door credited later (2026-09-05) -> 253.89 (it carries the most recent credit and pairs); no door-side credit row -> 0; credit on a door whose program is military -> 0; paired door cancelled -> 0; no door and no credit -> 0; cancelled zero-interest door account first -> 161.27. No probe raises an error. Scored values (161.27, 1719.48), every figure and the GT steps are unchanged; tool signatures unchanged.

[Revisions — round 8] (audit revision_7, G18 residuals a-c; coordinator route-around) The extended bundle credit is now scoped to a household holding exactly one Ridgeline door contract that is not cancelled (counted exactly: one XCOUNT per non-cancelled status summed); for such a household the paired door is that door (read by status filter, unique within the scope), and the credit arises when it was signed within the bundle window of this contract (DAYS between the two dates), its discount program is none and this contract's is none. Both overwrites' replaced_by now name that scope, so the base grant clause and base amount stay in force verbatim for every other household (a household with two or more live door contracts gets, under base, one credit per in-window pair of the series bundle percentage of the signed price; this policy figures none for it). Window contracts need no count: with one door, each window contract's single credit is exactly its pair with that door, as the base per-pair rule grants. The door-side credit row is no longer read (it stays as consistent history). The deposit prerequisite sentence and its condition carry the same scope, and for every other household the deposit balance is worked out on the credits already on the ledger. Tool signature changed: post_door_bundle_credit_ed16c33c now takes door_contract_id (Id class, from the door contract lookup) as part of the credit's reference, so credits for two pairs granted on the same day under the base rule stay separate entries; task 1's gold call (step 8) now passes RD-26-137715's id. This world sits inside the scope (one door contract, measured; one window contract). Probe table: gold -> 161.27; single door out of window (2026-05-01) -> 0; cancelled second door present -> 161.27; two live doors -> 0 from this policy (base rule applies); two live window contracts with one door -> 161.27 on W1 and 80.78 on the second; no door -> 0; door program military -> 0; single door closed 2018 -> 0. Scored values (161.27, 1719.48), every figure and the GT steps are unchanged.

[Revisions — round 9] (render-source window_round1 F4) The credit-basis sentence now states that the largest count is used should more than one completed final measure be recorded, as the compute (MAX) and the window-project step already did; this world has one completed final measure (14 openings). Scored values (161.27, 1719.48), every figure, the GT steps and the tool signatures are unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Elena Dorsey, fifty-five, a hospital pharmacist who lives at 141 Grandin Road in Cincinnati. This summer you signed up with Ridgeline for fourteen replacement windows, signed at your kitchen table on August 31. In July you had already bought a fiberglass sliding patio door from the Ridgeline showroom. After the windows were measured you added a color for the outside of the frames, grilles and triple-pane glass. The salesperson told you that with the color upgrade you would need to put more down on the deposit before the window order can go to the factory. You are calling to pay whatever is left of the deposit on the windows contract, today, with your debit card, so the order is not held up. You do not know the figure and expect the representative to tell you. You are brisk and organized, a little short on time, and you like a clear number.
You give details only when asked. To find your account you give your phone number, 5135550113; for a second detail your email, elena.dorsey1@gmail.com; if more is needed, your ZIP code 45208 and your date of birth 1971-09-30. If asked for the window contract number you read RW-26-131058 off your copy; the patio door contract is RD-26-137715. If asked how the door is being paid for, you say it is on a Ridgeline financing plan; the windows you are paying yourself. You do not know anything about discounts or how deposits are calculated.
If the representative tells you something has to be put on the windows account before the deposit can be figured, you say go ahead, as long as they tell you what it is. When the representative tells you the amount and hands the payment over to you, you pay exactly that amount with your debit card (a card payment) and read back the confirmation if asked. Once the payment shows as recorded you thank them and hang up; you do not bring up anything else.
